data.short_description: Public university in Normal, Alabama, US
data.extract: Alabama Agricultural and Mechanical University is a public historically black land-grant university in Normal, Alabama, United States, a part of Huntsville. Founded in 1875 as a state-run "normal school", it took its present name in 1969. AAMU is a member-school of the Thurgood Marshall College Fund and is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools. The Alabama Agricultural and Mechanical University Historic District, also known as Normal Hill College Historic District, has 28 buildings and four structures listed in the United States National Register of Historic Places. Alabama A&M's athletic teams, known as the Bulldogs, compete in NCAA Division I as members of the Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC).

awards.title: ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL AND MECHANICAL UNIVERSITY (AAMU) IS A PUBLIC, COMPREHENSIVE 1890 LAND-GRANT INSTITUTION, COMMITTED TO ACCESS AND OPPORTUNITY, DEDICATED TO INTELLECTUAL INQUIRY, SERVICE, AND IS RESPONSIVE TO THE NEEDS OF A DIVERSE STUDENT POPULATION AND THE SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC NEEDS OF THE STATE AND REGION. AS A CENTER OF EXCELLENCE, THE UNIVERSITY IS DEDICATED TO PROVIDING A STUDENT-CENTERED EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT, SERVING THE GENERAL PUBLIC THROUGH COOPERATIVE EXTENSION, AND CONDUCTING RESEARCH FOR THE EMERGENCE OF SCHOLARS, SCIENTISTS, LEADERS, AND CRITICAL THINKERS WHO ARE EQUIPPED TO EXCEL IN A 21ST CENTURY GLOBAL SOCIETY. THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL, LIFE AND NATURAL SCIENCES (CALNS) OPERATES IN THE TRADITIONAL LAND-GRANT CONCEPT WITH INSTRUCTIONAL, RESEARCH AND OUTREACH PROGRAMS. CALNS IS CHALLENGING STEREOTYPICAL CONCEPTIONS OF AGRICULTURAL, LIFE AND NATURAL SCIENCES AS IT PREPARES STUDENTS TO EXCEL IN A CHANGING WORLD WITH CERTAIN CORE PROFICIENCIES. COLLEGE FRESHMEN OFTHE FIRST DECADES OF THE 21ST CENTURY WILL REPRESENT THE WORK FORCE THROUGH THE MIDDLE OF THE TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY.NOTABLY, ALABAMA A&M UNIVERSITY IS COMMITTED TO DESIGNING ITS CURRICULA, DIRECTING ITS RESEARCH, AND SERVING THE COMMUNITY THROUGH EXTENSION PROGRAMS THAT PREPARE STUDENTS AND PROFESSIONALS WHO WILL MEET PROFICIENCIES AND THE WORKFORCE CHALLENGES OF THIS CENTURY. THE OVERARCHING NEED IS FOR CALNS TO MAINTAIN AND ADVANCE THESE PROFICIENCIES THROUGH CONTINUOUS FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT IMPROVEMENTS. THE EXTENSION PROGRAM IS A UNIFIED EFFORT BETWEEN ALABAMA A&M UNIVERSITY AND AUBURN UNIVERSITY BASED ON A FEDERAL MANDATE REGARDING EXTENSION PROGRAMMING IN ALABAMA. EXTENSION PROGRAMS THAT ARE OPERATED THROUGH THE LEADERSHIP AT AAMU REMAIN INTEGRATED WITHIN THE COLLEGE'S PROGRAMS AND ACTIVITIES AND CONTINUE TO USE RESEARCH-BASED KNOWLEDGE CONTENT FROM CALNS AS WELL AS OTHER SOURCES INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL TO THE UNIVERSITY. THE EXTENSION PROGRAM IS COMMITTED TO ASSISTING ALABAMA'S FAMILIES, COMMUNITIES, ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS THROUGH THE ENHANCEMENT AND EXPANSION OF FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT RESOURCES, WITH A GREATER ROLE THE SOCIAL MEDIA AND WEBINARS, AND ONLINE WORKSHOPS AS WELL AS THE ADVANCES IN AGRICULTURE ALSO ASSIDUOUSLY ADDRESS CORE NIFA CHALLENGE AREAS IN FOOD SECURITY, CLIMATE VARIABILITY AND CHANGE, WATER, SUSTAINABLE BIOENERGY, CHILDHOOD OBESITY PREVENTION AND FOOD SAFETY.THE TRIAD FOCI OF TEACHING, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION ARE BOTH COLLECTIVELY AND INDIVIDUALLY POISED TO EXPAND THE FRONTIERS OF AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES, FOOD AND ANIMAL SCIENCES, BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES, URBAN AND REGIONAL PLANNING, AND FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES. AAMU'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES INCLUDES UPGRADING OF UNIVERSITY INFRASTRUCTURE AND FACILITIES TO ENHANCE ACADEMIC, RESEARCH AND OUTREACH ACTIVITIES AAMU/CALNS PROPOSED EFFORTS ARE IN CONSONANCE WITH EACH OF USDA-NIFA'S SIX NATIONAL CHALLENGE AREAS. THE RENOVATION OF SEVERAL BUILDINGS AND SPECIFIC STRUCTURES AND THE ACQUISITION OF EQUIPMENT THROUGH FACILITIES FUNDS, ADDRESS IN PART SOME OF THE NEEDS FOR PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT. TO EXPAND INFRASTRUCTURE AND EQUIPMENT NEEDS OF CALNS AND EXTENSION, CONTINUING SUPPORT THROUGH THE 1890 FACILITIES FUNDING WILL AUGMENT THE ONGOING EFFORTS BY THE INSTITUTION TO ENHANCE STUDENT LEARNING, CONDUCT CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH, AND CREATE AND IMPLEMENT VIRTUAL AND NONTRADITIONAL PROGRAMS FOR EXTENSION, RESEARCH AND INSTRUCTION.

awards.title: ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL AND MECHANICAL UNIVERSITY (AAMU) CONDUCTS RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT MEET THE NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF ALABAMA AND THE NATION. TO FULFILL OUR OBLIGATIONS UNDER THE USDANIFA EVANS ALLEN ACT OF 1890 (SECTION 1445) FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2026, THERE ARE SEVERAL PROJECTS BEING SUBMITTED FOR APPROVAL. RESEARCH AREAS OF INTEREST ARE: FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY; GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY; HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; AND COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING. ALL THESE ARE ALIGNED WITH THE USDA PRIORITIES.  FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY: RESEARCH AND EXTENSION-INTEGRATED ACTIVITIES ENHANCE FOOD SYSTEMS, FOOD SAFETY, AND AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY. THE GOAL OF THIS CRITICAL ISSUE IS TO DEVELOP TECHNOLOGY AND METHODS TO PROTECT AND ENHANCE THE SAFETY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, REDUCE EPIDEMICS OF FOOD-BORNE ILLNESSES, AND TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND METHODOLOGIES FOR RAPID DETECTION OF THREAT AGENTS, INCLUDING EXISTING AND EMERGING DISEASES OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS, RISK ASSESSMENT, AND FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY.  GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER: THE GOAL IS TO ENHANCE THE COMPETITIVENESS AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRIES IN ALABAMA THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF BEST PRACTICES OR TECHNOLOGIES. THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ADDRESSES TWO BROADLY DEFINED PRIORITY AREAS; I) PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION AND PLANT PRODUCTS, INCLUDING IMPROVED CROPPING SYSTEMS, PLANT BREEDING/GENOMICS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, PRECISION AGRICULTURE, AND ALTERNATIVE SPECIALTY CROPS; AND II) ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, INCLUDING IMPROVED FOOD-ANIMAL SYSTEMS AND STOCKS. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST ARE PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS THAT INCLUDE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES THAT PRESENT INNOVATIVE SYNERGIES OF DISCIPLINES AND PERSPECTIVES.  HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY: OBESITY, DIABETES, HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, AND VASCULAR ISSUES ARE MOSTLY CAUSED BY THE LACK OF NUTRIENTS, THE LACK OF EXERCISE, POOR LIFESTYLE CHOICES, AND STRESS OF THE INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS. AS A RESULT OF THE GROWING HEALTH CONCERNS FOR ALABAMA CITIZENS, THERE HAS BEEN A COMBINED EFFORT TO EDUCATE AND MOTIVATE CITIZENS THROUGHOUT THE STATE TO MAKE BETTER HEALTH DECISIONS. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF ALABAMIANS, TARGETING LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES, THROUGH CHRONIC DISEASE AWARENESS, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, NUTRITION EDUCATION, HEALTH LITERACY, AND ACCESS TO AND CONSUMPTION OF FRESH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY: THIS PROGRAM PLAN WILL GENERATE KNOWLEDGE TO MANAGE AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL SYSTEMS IN WAYS THAT SUPPORT ENERGY INDEPENDENCE, RESOURCE EFFICIENCY, AND RURAL ECONOMIC GROWTH. SPECIFIC AREAS INCLUDE: SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, ENERGY UTILIZATION STRATEGIES (INCLUDING AGRICULTURAL WASTE-TO-ENERGY CONVERSION); WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, SOIL HEALTH ENHANCEMENT, AND PRECISION AGRICULTURE. REMOTE SENSING AND TECHNOLOGY-DRIVEN APPROACHES WILL BE PRIORITIZED TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY, REDUCE COSTS, AND ENSURE LONG-TERM RESOURCE SECURITY. ENVIRONMENTAL INITIATIVES WILL BE FRAMED AROUND SUPPORTING ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY, RURAL-URBAN INTERFACE SOLUTIONS, AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE.  COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING: THIS AREA IS DESIGNED TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH RURAL AND URBAN PLANNING PROGRAMS. APPROPRIATED FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR EXPENSES IN RESEARCH, WHICH WILL INCLUDE FACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES, STUDENT SUPPORT, DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, ADMINISTRATIVE PLANNING AND DIRECTION, EQUIPMENT PURCHASE AND MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPLIES PURCHASE (AMONG OTHER APPROVED SPENDING).

COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING: THIS AREA IS DESIGNED TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH RURAL AND URBAN PLANNING PROGRAMS. APPROPRIATED FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR EXPENSES IN CONDUCTING RESEARCH TO INCLUDE FACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES, STUDENT SUPPORT, DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, ADMINISTRATIVE PLANNING AND DIRECTION, EQUIPMENT PURCHASE AND MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPLIES PURCHASE (AMONG OTHER APPROVED SPENDING).

awards.title: ALABAMA A<(>&<)>M UNIVERSITY MCINTIRE-STENNIS FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM INCLUDES SILVICULTURAL  STRATEGIES FOR RESTORING MIXED PINE-HARDWOOD FOREST AND NATIVE GRASSES, DETECTING RARE AND  ENDANGERED WILDLIFE SPECIES, ECOLOGICAL PATTERNS OF FOREST DYNAMICS, EFFECTS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT  ON AQUATIC AND TERRESTRIAL BIOINDICATORS, IMPROVED FOREST OPERATIONS, AND MINORITY PARTICIPATION IN  OUTDOOR RECREATION. MOST OF OUR RESEARCH IS CONDUCTED IN COLLABORATION WITH THE USDA FOREST  SERVICE, SOUTHERN RESEARCH STATION, NATIONAL FORESTS IN ALABAMA, AND (FIA) FOREST INVENTORY  AND ANALYSIS.WE ARE QUANTIFYING THE OCCURRENCE, CHARACTERISTICS, AND MANAGEMENT OF PINEHARDWOOD  FORESTS IN THE NORTH ALABAMA REGION, ASSESSING THEIR ECOLOGICAL AND ECONOMIC  IMPORTANCE, AND ESTABLISHING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PRODUCTIVITY AND DIVERSITY AND THE IMPACT  OF RECREATION AND OTHER HUMAN INFLUENCES ON THE TRENDS IN REGENERATION AND SPECIES COMPOSITION.  OTHER OBJECTIVES INCLUDE INVESTIGATING THE BEHAVIOR, USE PATTERNS, AND PARTICIPATION LEVELS IN  RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES BY VISITORS TO THE BANKHEAD NATIONAL FOREST AND IDENTIFYING THE FACTORS  WHICH LIMIT THE USE OF THE WILDERNESS AREAS BY MINORITIES. ECOLOGICAL GEOMETRY IS SEARCHED IN  FOREST STRUCTURES AND FUNCTIONS. THROUGH PERIODIC MONITORING OF ABUNDANCE, SPECIES OF TREE  INDIVIDUALS, AND THEIR GROWTH RATES AT DIFFERENT FORESTS (INCLUDING MIXED BROADLEAVED FORESTS AND  PINE PLANTATIONS) ACROSS SPATIAL SCALES BY GROUND MONITORING, REMOTE SENSING, AND GIS DATA,  INDICES OF ECOLOGICAL GEOMETRY ARE DEVELOPED TO STUDY THE SPATIAL-TEMPORAL DYNAMICS IN FOREST  STRUCTURE AND FUNCTIONS. THE IMPLICATIONS OF ECOLOGICAL GEOMETRY IN FOREST MANAGEMENT WILL BE  EXPLORED IN RESTORATION, PRESCRIBED BURNING, AND HARVESTING. SHORTLEAF PINE'S LACK OF NATURAL  REGENERATION IS A FOREST CONSERVATION ISSUE THAT NEEDS PROPER ATTENTION TO RESTORE THE SPECIES. WE  EXPECT THIS PROJECT TO GATHER VALUABLE DATA ON THE NATURAL REGENERATION OF SHORTLEAF PINE IN THE  FORESTS WITHIN ITS GEOGRAPHIC RANGE. WE WILL DETERMINE OPTIMAL SHORTLEAF PINE DENSITY LEVELS FOR  RE-ESTABLISHMENT SPECIES IN THE CENTRAL HARDWOOD REGION AND EXAMINE HOW CROP TREES AND SEED  PRODUCTION IMPACT SHORTLEAF PINE NATURAL REGENERATION.OUR FOCUS IS ALSO ON FOREST RESTORATION AND  THE EFFECTS OF MANAGEMENT ON FISH AND WILDLIFE DOWNSTREAM FROM THINNED AND PRESCRIBED BURNED  LOBLOLLY PINE FOREST SITES. SMALL MAMMALS, INCLUDING BATS, ARE CAPTURED OR HAVE ECHOLOCATION CALLS  MONITORED. AQUATIC MACROI NVERTEBRATES AND FISH ARE ALSO INVENTORIED QUARTERLY. WATER QUALITY AND  CHANNEL MORPHOLOGY PARAMETERS ARE ALSO MEASURED. WE ALSO SURVEYED FERAL SWINE ACTIVITY IN  RESPONSE TO PRESCRIBED BURNING IN UPSTREAM PINE STANDS. FERAL SWINE ROOTING ACTIVITY IS ALSO  INVESTIGATED AS A SOIL DISTURBANCE FACTOR THAT COULD AFFECT STREAM WATER QUALITY AND THE PRESENCE  AND ABUNDANCE OF AQUATIC SPECIES, SMALL MAMMALS, AND BATS AS BIOINDICATORS OF ENVIRONMENTAL  INTEGRITY IN DOWNSTREAM COMMUNITIES. PRESCRIBED FOREST FIRES AND THINNING PRACTICES ALSO AFFECT  THE AMPHIBIAN AND REPTILE COMMUNITIES. WE WANT TO UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISMS AND FUNCTIONAL  RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN FOREST HABITAT CHANGES AND HERPETOFAUNAL DIVERSITY AND STRUCTURE,  PARTICULARLY FROM LONG-TERM PERSPECTIVES.THIS STUDY'S PRIMARY PURPOSE IS TO UNDERSTAND BETTER  FACTORS AFFECTING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND GROWTH OF PLANTED NATIVE GRASSES, PARTICULARLY FACTORS THAT  DEVELOP OR ALTER DURING TIMBER HARVESTING. WE ASSESS HOW SOIL DISTURBANCE AND REMOVING OR  RETAINING LOGGING SLASH MAY AFFECT THE SURVIVAL AND GROWTH OF NATIVE GRASSES SUCH AS THE BIG  BLUESTEM GRASS.
